title: Telegram Bot API Token: Free Tools, Real Trade-offs
meta_description: What does Telegram Bot API Token cost in 2026 (spoiler: nothing), and how do you set it up properly? Covers free tiers, open-source alternatives and honest…
intro: Most 'complete guides' to telegram bot api token pad the word count with ads. This one is different: every recommendation below runs on a free tier, an open-source project, or both. If a recommendation ever costs money, we say so in plain words.

We'll walk through Telegram Bot API, Bluesky At Protocol, Mastodon API, and Automate the boring parts — and finish with the questions people actually ask, so you can check before you buy anything. You shouldn't have to buy anything.

sections.heading: Telegram Bot API
paragraphs: First, the thing that actually matters: The Telegram Bot API is free, HTTP-based and needs nothing but a token from @BotFather.

Concretely: Create a bot in one message, then send and receive messages, create channels, and drive webhooks entirely over plain HTTPS. It is the cheapest 'social media' channel a self-publishing site can own, and this blog posts to it when a token is configured.
If you only do one thing today, make it this one.
bullets: Message @BotFather and /newbot to get a token
Optionally set a webhook with setWebhook for incoming events

sections.heading: Bluesky At Protocol
paragraphs: First, the thing that actually matters: Bluesky runs on the open AT Protocol, whose public API is free — an account plus an app password is all a bot needs to post.

Which, in day-to-day terms, means: createSession returns an access token, and app.bsky.feed.post publishes a post. No middleman, no paid 'basic tier' for your own account's posting, and the protocol is openly specified so the implementation is boring in the best way.
Keep it this simple and you'll be ahead of most tutorials out there.

sections.heading: Mastodon API
paragraphs: Here's the part most people get wrong. Mastodon's API is free and fully documented — any instance lets you register an app and post programmatically.

In other words: Create an app in your instance's developer settings, exchange it for a token, and the REST API handles statuses, follows and search. Because the whole platform is open source and federated, posting to it costs nothing and can point at an instance you run yourself.
Keep it this simple and you'll be ahead of most tutorials out there.

sections.heading: Automate the boring parts
paragraphs: Start with the basics. Anything you do twice by hand should become a script. That's the entire discipline of free automation.

So what does that look like when you're actually doing it? A cron expression, a webhook, or a scheduled workflow costs nothing to run and buys back an hour every week. Start with one small automation — a nightly backup, a feed check, a deploy on push — and add more only when the first one proves itself.
Write down what you change and why — your future self will thank you.

faq.answer: Mastodon's API is free and fully documented — any instance lets you register an app and post programmatically. Treat that as the working assumption and re-check the docs once a quarter.
